features.title: Exact fixed-point length on a 1/1024-inch grid
features.acceptance: Length.Inches(3, 1, 2) has Units == 3584, equals Length.FeetInches(0, 3, 1, 2), and Length.UnitsPerInch is 1024.

features.title: Every tape, lumber and table value the design names is exact
features.acceptance: 1/16in, 3 1/2in, 23/32in, 15/32in, 5/4 decking at 1in, 16in and 24in on-centre and 6ft-0in each construct, read back unchanged, and 6ft-0in <= 6ft-0in is true (the comparison integer millimetres broke in issue #4).

features.title: Rounding is always explicit and arithmetic is checked
features.acceptance: Divide and Scale take a Rounding argument; 1in Divide 3 gives 341 units, TryDivideExact(3) returns false and TryDivideExact(4) returns 1/4in; a sum past long.MaxValue throws OverflowException instead of wrapping.

features.title: Feet-inch-fraction text parses and formats, reporting any rounding
features.acceptance: 6'-3 5/16", 6' 3-5/16", 6ft 3in, 75 5/16, 75.3125, 3/4 and -1/2 parse to the expected Length while mm, cm, empty and malformed text are rejected; 1/3 and 3.505 parse with wasRounded true and 3.5 with it false; formatting reduces 8/16 to 1/2, carries 12in to 1'-0", keeps a negative sign, and reports IsExact false for a 1/32in value shown at 1/16in.

features.title: Angles are integer arcseconds with exact right angles
features.acceptance: Angle.Degrees(22, 30) equals Degrees(22) + Degrees(0, 30); Angle.Right rotated three times has IsRightAngleMultiple true and QuarterTurns 3; Degrees(45) has IsRightAngleMultiple false.

features.title: Box corners derive exactly from stored parameters
features.acceptance: For each of the four right-angle rotations, a Box with a given anchor, width and height derives all four corners and its centre by integer arithmetic, with no value off the grid except an odd-span centre.

features.title: A sketch validates its own referential integrity
features.acceptance: Sketch.Validate() reports a dangling entity or relationship reference, a box with zero or negative width or height, and two structurally identical relationships, each naming the offending id.

features.title: One relationship checker decides exact versus tolerance
features.acceptance: RelationshipChecker classifies every relationship kind and computes its residual; exact-class kinds are checked at zero tolerance whatever Tolerances is passed, and a test recomputes Tolerances.Position from Length.UnitsPerInch so a change to the grid cannot leave it stale.

features.title: An exact request propagates through the relationship graph
features.acceptance: SetParameter on a box's driving width relationship keeps the anchor and moves the far edge, and a box held Flush against that edge translates by the same delta with its own size unchanged.

features.title: The anchor rule, and conflicts that name their cause
features.acceptance: Resizing a box whose far side is Flush to an anchored box moves the anchor side instead; when both sides are pinned the result is OverConstrained naming both Anchored relationships and the Flush, and the input sketch is returned unchanged.

features.title: Drag is best effort and reports what it applied
features.acceptance: Dragging a box held Flush on a vertical edge to an anchored box returns Solved with AppliedDelta zero in X and the full requested Y; a drag blocked on both axes is Solved with a zero delta, never OverConstrained.

features.title: A malformed request is rejected, not reported as a conflict
features.acceptance: Adding a Parallel relationship, dragging an edge whose size a ParamValue drives, and rotating a box that carries relationships each return Rejected with the named reason and an unchanged sketch; a SetParameter naming a relationship the sketch does not have returns Rejected(UnknownRelationship).

features.title: Structural edits cascade, demote and batch atomically
features.acceptance: Removing a box removes the relationships referencing it and the dimensions measuring it and lists all of them in the change set; removing a driving relationship leaves its dimension in place with Drives null; a Batch whose second request conflicts applies nothing and returns that request's report.

features.title: The updater is never silently inconsistent
features.acceptance: Over generated rectilinear sketches, properties P1-P8 and P10 of the design doc hold: every result is Rejected or OverConstrained with the input unchanged, or Succeeded with a sketch that passes Validate and the checker with no violations.

features.title: Read a plain scene file into a sketch
features.acceptance: Loading a sample scene.json produces a Sketch whose entities, relationships and layers equal the file's contents by value, with lengths and angles read as integers in the declared units.

features.title: Loading is strict and never repairs
features.acceptance: A file with an unknown field, a dangling id, a decimal length, or a relationship kind the running updater does not support is refused with a message naming the field, id or kind; nothing is opened approximately.

features.title: Loading re-checks the file's own relationships
features.acceptance: A file whose stored geometry does not satisfy its stored relationships is refused with the violating relationship ids listed.

features.title: Exact format-version match, no migration
features.acceptance: The loader accepts only the formatVersion the app writes; a file one version older and a file one version newer both fail before the scene is parsed, with a message naming the file's version and the app's.

features.title: The manifest records what the file means
features.acceptance: A saved project's manifest.json carries formatVersion, the app version, the storage units (inch/1024 and arcsecond) and the project's adopted code, which is null when none is chosen.

features.title: The project is a documented zip container
features.acceptance: A saved project opens with a standard zip tool and contains manifest.json, scene.json, a thumbnail and an assets directory, matching the format document committed in the repository.

features.title: Save then load is an identity
features.acceptance: For every sketch the generator produces, Load(Save(sketch)) equals sketch by value (property P9 of the design doc).

features.title: Nominal lumber resolves to actual dimensions
features.acceptance: Looking up 2x4 returns 1 1/2in by 3 1/2in as exact Length values and 4x4 returns 3 1/2in by 3 1/2in, alongside the stock lengths and stud spacings the library carries for each size.

features.title: Sheet goods resolve to actual thickness and sheet size
features.acceptance: A nominal 3/4in sheet resolves to the actual thickness its cited source gives, and the standard sheet size is returned as two exact Lengths.

features.title: Decking and fasteners resolve from data
features.acceptance: Decking nominal-to-actual sizes and fastener entries (gauge, length, penny size) are returned from the shipped data files, with no value hardcoded in the lookup code.

features.title: Every reference table cites the standard it was authored from
features.acceptance: Each table in the library carries a source citation naming the standard or specification consulted (for example ALSC PS 20 for softwood lumber sizes), and a test fails any table whose citation is missing or empty.

features.title: Adding a material is a data change
features.acceptance: The shipped data files load through the same reader the app uses, a malformed or duplicate entry fails the load with the file and entry named, and no code change is needed to add a nominal size.

features.title: A part resolves its stock through the materials library
features.acceptance: A part declared as 2x4 reports cut dimensions of 1 1/2in by 3 1/2in taken from the materials library, never the nominal name.

features.title: The cut list reads stored parameters, not derived corners
features.acceptance: A part typed as 10in wide and then rotated lists as 10in in the cut list, read from Box.Width rather than from the distance between derived corners.

features.title: The cut list groups identical parts
features.acceptance: Four identical legs appear as one row with quantity 4, and every row carries final dimensions, quantity and material.

features.title: The coffee-table cut list matches hand-computed expectations
features.acceptance: The coffee-table fixture's cut list equals, row for row, the expectations file computed by hand from the fixture's dimensions independently of the implementation.

features.title: The shopping list matches hand-computed expectations
features.acceptance: The stocked-bench fixture (the shopping list's worked example: the coffee table names no stock and is not edited) aggregates to the expectations file's stock counts (boards and sheets; nothing in the model references a fastener yet), and parts that fit within one board still report one board to buy while the cut list reports each part.

features.title: Takeoff totals are grouped and rounded once
features.acceptance: Board feet and sheet counts are grouped by material and thickness, computed from exact lengths and rounded once at the end rather than per part.

features.title: Pan the view without moving anything
features.acceptance: Panning by wheel, by drag and by keyboard changes the view transform only; every entity's stored coordinates are byte-identical before and after.

features.title: Zoom about the cursor, and zoom to fit
features.acceptance: A wheel tick keeps the model point under the pointer fixed to within one pixel, and the fit command frames every entity's bounding box with a visible margin for both a single entity and the sample design.

features.title: Y is up in model space
features.acceptance: A model point with the larger Y draws higher on screen, and the screen flip appears in the view transform and nowhere else in the drawing code.

features.title: Dimension labels are computed, never cached
features.acceptance: A dimension renders its value from the geometry it measures, formatted as feet, inches and fractions by Core.Geometry's Format, and the rendered text changes when that geometry changes.

features.title: Every edit goes through the update interface
features.acceptance: A pointer drag issues Drag or DragEdge, a typed value issues SetParameter or AddRelationship(ParamValue), a compound gesture issues one Batch, and no UI code path constructs a Sketch directly.

features.title: A snap creates a stored relationship the canvas can show
features.acceptance: Snapping to a grid, endpoint, midpoint, intersection, perpendicular or parallel target creates the corresponding stored relationship and displays it; the canvas offers only the kinds in the updater's SupportedRelationships and infers nothing from position.

features.title: Live dimensions follow the geometry while dragging
features.acceptance: While a drag is in progress the dimension bound to the dragged edge updates on each pointer move and reads the same value as the geometry when the drag ends.

features.title: Every update result has a place on screen
features.acceptance: OverConstrained shows the conflict report's summary and highlights the named relationships, Rejected explains its reason in plain words, and UnderConstrained appears at most as a hint and never as an error.

features.title: Undo, redo and layers over immutable sketch values
features.acceptance: Undo restores the previous Sketch value exactly, one Batch is one undo step, entity ids survive so the selection is preserved, and a SetLayer change is undoable like any other.

features.title: Display precision is per project, and inexact display is marked
features.acceptance: Lengths display at the project's chosen denominator from 1 to 64, rounding half away from zero, and a value whose displayed text is not the stored value is marked (for example with a leading approximation sign).

features.title: Adopted-code packs load from data
features.acceptance: The engine loads a pack from its data directory and reports its jurisdiction, base model code and in-force date, with no pack named in the engine's code.

features.title: Every result carries a full citation
features.acceptance: A sized result carries the state, adopted code, table and row it came from, and a test fails any result whose citation is missing a part.

features.title: Out of scope is a first-class result
features.acceptance: Inputs past a table's limits return OutOfScope carrying the citation of the limit that was exceeded; the result type is a closed union with no third case, so no silent failure is representable.

features.title: The header evaluator returns the matching row
features.acceptance: Given a wall context and an opening spec that the loaded pack's header table covers, the evaluator returns that row's header and jack and king stud counts, identified by the row it used.

features.title: The bracing evaluator runs over a whole wall line
features.acceptance: Given a wall line's solid segments (from its openings), the bracing method a person assigned to each, and the site, the evaluator reports whether the pack's required braced length is met, cites the section it applied, and re-runs whenever an opening on that line changes.

features.title: Overlays compose, and the citation names the layer
features.acceptance: A state amendment overlaid on a base model code produces a result whose citation names the layer that supplied the value, and a row the state did not amend cites the base layer.

features.title: The code picker is built from the installed packs
features.acceptance: The picker lists exactly the installed packs, each by jurisdiction, base model code and in-force date, with no list hardcoded in the app, and the chosen pack is stored in the project manifest and survives save and reopen.

features.title: Changing the project's code recomputes every result
features.acceptance: Switching a project from one installed pack to another recomputes every rules result in the project against the new pack and re-flags any result that no longer holds, with no stale result or stale citation carried over.

features.title: Connecticut 2026 header and fastener tables
features.acceptance: Every row encoded for the header-span and fastener-schedule tables matches the state's published adopted text, and each test names the page or section it was read from.

features.title: Connecticut 2026 boundary rows flip cleanly
features.acceptance: For each limit in the encoded tables, an input just inside returns a sized result and an input just outside returns out of scope citing that limit, with the boundary values taken from the state's published adopted text.

features.title: Connecticut 2026 bracing provisions
features.acceptance: Every row encoded for the wall-bracing provisions matches the state's published adopted text, cited by page or section.

features.title: Connecticut 2022 pack
features.acceptance: Every row encoded for the header-span, bracing and fastener tables matches the 2022 state code's published adopted text, cited by page or section, and differs from the 2026 pack wherever that text does.

features.title: Massachusetts 780 CMR residential pack
features.acceptance: Every encoded row matches the state's published adopted text, including the site criteria the state sets for itself, cited by page or section.

features.title: Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code pack
features.acceptance: Every encoded row matches the state's published adopted text, cited by page or section, and the older-code transition rule is encoded only after it has been read in the Pennsylvania Code itself.

features.title: A municipal overlay changes only what it amends
features.acceptance: A municipal amendment overlaid on the state pack changes exactly the rows the ordinance amends, leaves every other row identical to the state pack, and its citation names the ordinance.

features.title: Wall attributes are entered, never defaulted
features.acceptance: A wall with no ground snow load, wind speed or seismic design category entered cannot be evaluated; the app asks for the missing input and names it, rather than substituting a value.

features.title: An opening is geometrically bound to its wall
features.acceptance: An opening is a box held Flush on the wall's two long edges with an AxisDistance from a wall corner, so moving or resizing the wall moves the opening with it and the opening slides when the AxisDistance changes.

features.title: The header result is live
features.acceptance: Resizing or moving an opening re-runs the header lookup, and the displayed header, stud counts and citation change with it rather than keeping the previous result.

features.title: Out of scope routes to an engineer, never to a number
features.acceptance: An opening whose span or site inputs fall outside the loaded pack's tables shows the out-of-scope message with the limit's citation and shows no header size at all.

features.title: Enlarging an opening rechecks the wall line's bracing
features.acceptance: With the bracing method already on each of the wall line's segments entered by the user, enlarging an opening past what the line can carry flags the wall, naming the section applied and the shortfall.

features.title: Walls join at corners from their exact corners
features.acceptance: Two walls whose end lies on the other's long face, whose ends meet, or which overlap at a corner join; offset by one unit (1/1024 in) they do not; the plan draws a joined pair with no seam; an opening reaching into a joined wall's thickness is refused naming that wall.

features.title: A wall bounds a room by a flush face
features.acceptance: A wall whose long face lies on the line of a room edge and overlaps it bounds the room; its openings inside the edge are the room's, one straddling the edge's end is not; a room with no bounding wall takes off its own perimeter and says openings are not subtracted.

features.title: The code check is routed by the wall's side and bearing
features.acceptance: An exterior bearing wall asks the exterior-bearing table, an interior bearing wall the interior-bearing table (No data naming it when the pack has none); a wall marked not bearing is Not checked and takes the header the person chose, said to be their choice; a side or bearing not said is an input missing naming it.

features.title: The framing diff says what is new and what comes out
features.acceptance: A new window in an existing 12 ft wall lists 2 kings, 2 jacks, the header, the sill and 4 cripples as new and 2 studs out, assuming a regular 16 in layout; a new wall is all new, a demolished wall all out, a closed-up window fills with studs, an unchanged existing wall is on neither list.

features.title: The area takeoff is exact and rounds once per line
features.acceptance: For the 12 x 14 ft basement room: 18 drywall sheets from one pool, 10 bags of insulation, 4 gallons of paint, 185 sq ft and 10 boxes of flooring with the 10 % allowance, 7 sticks of baseboard; with no coverage typed each line shows the area and says what to type.

features.title: A measured room reports out of square without redrawing
features.acceptance: Unequal opposite sides or diagonals read out of square; one diagonal is compared by its square exactly; a true 12 x 16 ft room with a 20 ft diagonal is not flagged; the takeoff stays on the drawn size and says so.

features.title: Insulation by stud bays counts the full-height bays
features.acceptance: The basement room's four framed walls have 37 full-height bays, 7'-7 1/2" tall; a wall napkin does not frame has none and is named.

features.title: A survey underlay calibrates from two known points
features.acceptance: After placing an image, clicking two points a known distance apart and entering that distance, a measurement between those two points on the canvas reads the entered value.

features.title: Property lines and setbacks measure against structures
features.acceptance: Property lines and their setback offsets draw over the underlay, and the distance from a placed structure to each line is reported in feet, inches and fractions.

features.title: North arrow and sheet orientation are stored with the project
features.acceptance: The site plan's north direction is stored as an exact Angle in the project file and survives save and reopen.

features.title: Ledger attachment is sized from the project's pack
features.acceptance: Given the ledger size, the band joist it attaches to and the tributary load inputs, the fastener type and spacing come from the loaded pack's adopted provisions with a citation, or out of scope when the connection is outside them.

features.title: Joist and beam spans come from the adopted tables
features.acceptance: Given species, size, spacing and span, the result is the matching row of the loaded pack's adopted span provisions with a citation, or out of scope, and every encoded row matches that state's published adopted text.

features.title: Footings are sized from tributary area and entered soil bearing
features.acceptance: Given a tributary area and a user-entered soil bearing value, the footing size comes from the loaded pack's adopted table with a citation, or out of scope; the soil value is never defaulted.

features.title: Guards and stairs follow the adopted provisions
features.acceptance: A deck surface above the pack's guard trigger height requires a guard with the section cited, and a stair layout from deck height to grade either satisfies the pack's rise and run provisions or returns out of scope.

features.title: A deck produces a cut list through the furniture machinery
features.acceptance: A framed deck produces a cut list and a materials list through the same code path as a furniture project, with framing and decking members resolved through the materials library.

features.title: Exported DXF opens in another CAD tool
features.acceptance: An exported AC1015 file opens in at least one of QCAD, LibreCAD or FreeCAD with every entity at the same model coordinates it had in napkin, and an R12 fallback export opens likewise.

features.title: Exported dimensions are literal geometry
features.acceptance: The exported file contains dimension lines, arrowheads and text as ordinary entities and contains no associative DIMENSION entity.

features.title: PDF sheets are vector and true scale, with a title block
features.acceptance: A part 24in long measures 24in at the sheet's stated scale when measured in a PDF reader, the page contains vector path operators rather than an embedded raster image, and every sheet carries the project name, scale, date and the tool's disclaimer.

features.title: Self-contained builds start on a clean machine
features.acceptance: The published Windows and macOS builds launch on a machine with no .NET runtime installed and open the sample design.

features.title: First-run instructions and the source offer ship with every build
features.acceptance: The README documents the macOS System Settings path for opening an unsigned app and the Windows SmartScreen path with every URL reachable, and each published artifact contains the AGPL-3.0 text and a written offer of source naming the commit it was built from.

features.title: A tag produces downloadable macOS and Windows artifacts
features.acceptance: Pushing a tag matching the release pattern builds a macOS artifact and a Windows artifact and attaches both to a GitHub release created for that tag.

features.title: Every release is a pre-release
features.acceptance: The release the pipeline creates has the pre-release flag set and is not marked latest, and a test over the workflow definition fails if that flag is ever removed.

features.title: The arm64 macOS artifact carries its ad-hoc signature only
features.acceptance: The published macOS arm64 binary verifies as carrying the toolchain's automatic ad-hoc signature, which arm64 code needs to run at all, and carries no Developer ID signature or notarization ticket.

features.title: One version string, set in one place
features.acceptance: Every assembly and the running app report the same version, taken from a single property in the repository, with the commit SHA present in the informational version.

features.title: Angled golden cases solve and verify
features.acceptance: A mitered frame, a 45-degree brace between two rectilinear parts and a tapered leg each solve, are rounded once, repaired through the propagator and pass the relationship checker before the sketch is returned.

features.title: The solver is no worse on the direct updater's own domain
features.acceptance: Property P1 holds under the solver over the same generated rectilinear sketches the direct updater is tested on.

features.title: Solver conflict reports name relationships worth removing
features.acceptance: For each conflicting golden case the report names a set of relationships whose removal makes the same request succeed, and distinguishes a contradiction from a failure to converge.

features.title: Open a sample design and see it drawn
features.acceptance: Launch the app, open the coffee-table sample through the file dialog, and every part in the fixture appears on the canvas at the fixture's expected positions.

features.title: Pan with the wheel, a drag and the keyboard
features.acceptance: With the sample open, scroll the wheel, drag with the pan tool and press the arrow keys; the view origin readout changes for each and no entity's stored coordinates change.

features.title: Zoom about the cursor, then zoom to fit
features.acceptance: Wheel-zoom in over one corner of the sample so that most of it leaves the viewport, press the zoom-to-fit shortcut, and every entity is framed again with a margin.

features.title: Read dimension labels in feet, inches and fractions
features.acceptance: Open the wall-with-window sample, zoom in on the opening, and the dimension labels read the exact feet-inch-fraction strings the fixture's expectations file gives.

features.title: A file the app cannot read fails visibly
features.acceptance: With a design already open, try to open a scene file carrying an unknown field, a dangling id and an unsupported relationship kind; a message names what was wrong, and the design already on screen is untouched.

features.title: Rulers along the plan and a scale bar along the orthographic 3D view
features.acceptance: Open the coffee table: the plan has no rulers; View > Rulers ticks the item and draws feet-and-inch rulers from 0" with the toolbar stepped in clear of them; + pressed three times zooms in and the rulers read a finer step; V shows the 3D view in perspective with no scale bar and the toolbar back at its margins; O makes it orthographic with a scale bar labelled for the zoom, and O again takes the bar away; back in the plan, View > Rulers unticks the item, the rulers go and the toolbar returns to where it started.

features.title: The snap buttons look along each axis and step through a selected part's faces
features.acceptance: Open the coffee table: the four view-snap buttons are hidden in the plan; select a leg and V shows them in 3D; Look along Z looks from above and again from below, Y from the south, and X from the east and again from the west; Next surface steps through the leg's six faces, top first, each face centred in the view, then wraps to the top; with nothing selected it starts again from above, then the south; V back to the plan hides the buttons.

features.title: Draw a rectangle by dragging
features.acceptance: Press, drag and release on empty canvas; a part appears, its live dimensions track the pointer during the drag, and its final size equals the distance dragged.

features.title: Type a dimension in feet-inch-fraction text
features.acceptance: Select the part, focus the width field by keyboard, type 2'-6 1/2" and press Enter; the part resizes to exactly that value, the anchor corner stays put, and the label reads back the same text.

features.title: Recover from invalid dimension text
features.acceptance: Type 250mm into the same field and press Enter; an error appears, the part is unchanged, and typing a valid value immediately afterwards resizes it as normal.

features.title: Move a part until it snaps, and see the relationship
features.acceptance: Drag one part towards another until the flush snap engages and release; the parts are flush and a stored Flush relationship appears in the relationship list.

features.title: Undo and redo a chain of edits
features.acceptance: After five edits mixing drags and typed dimensions, five undo presses return the design to its starting state and five redo presses return it to the last state, with the selection preserved throughout.

features.title: Save a design, reopen it and find the same design
features.acceptance: Save the design to a new file, close it, reopen it from the file dialog, and every part, dimension and relationship matches what was saved.

features.title: See a conflict explained rather than a wrong number
features.acceptance: Pin two parts so their widths cannot both change, type a width that cannot hold, and the conflict summary appears naming the relationships involved while the design stays as it was.

features.title: Pick a shaped part, duplicate it and snap the copy
features.acceptance: Open File > Samples > Rounded-corner table: a click on the blank inside its rounded-off corner picks nothing and a click on the shape picks the top; D adds a selected copy with the same size, cuts and part, no new relationship and the original unmoved; dragging the copy until its edge catches the original's adds a flush between the two; Ctrl/Cmd+L lists the two shaped blanks as one row of two with a thumbnail of the shape, and only shaped rows have one.

features.title: Shape one part in the workshop and take the cut off again
features.acceptance: Ctrl/Cmd+N, R and a drag draw a plain rectangle; C opens the shape workshop on it, and 1x6 typed as its stock resizes the blank to the 1x6's width; dragging the south-west corner inward cuts it while the button is still down and leaves one corner cut of the dragged size, selected with its fields showing; Escape returns to the drawing with the part unmoved and its outline clipped where a click no longer hits the shape; Ctrl/Cmd+L shows the row with its thumbnail and a sentence naming the south-west corner; back in the workshop a click on the cut corner selects that cut, a typed setback changes only that setback, Full mitre sets both setbacks to the blank's width at 45°, and Delete takes the cut off, leaving a plain rectangle that is still a 1x6.

features.title: Undo reaches stock, duplicate, pin, delete and the shape workshop
features.acceptance: Ctrl/Cmd+N greys out Undo and Redo; a 2x4 dragged from the toolbox's lumber drawer, then D, P and Delete on the copy, are four steps to undo; Ctrl/Cmd+Z three times brings back the pinned copy, then the free copy, then the lone 2x4; a corner cut in the shape workshop (C) clears the redo stack, undo there takes the cut off with the workshop still open on the same part and redo puts it back; two more undos take the cut and the placed part away, close the workshop and grey out Undo again.

features.title: Build the coffee table end to end
features.acceptance: Draw the top, four legs and the aprons using drags, snapping and typed dimensions, ending with geometry that matches the coffee-table fixture.

features.title: Assign materials to parts
features.acceptance: A floating toolbox groups stock by category (dimensional lumber, sheet goods, hardwood, fasteners) with one icon per category; choosing a category opens a text list of its items; hovering an item shows its actual size and citation before it is placed; placing one sets the part's stock reference.

features.title: Open the cut list and check it
features.acceptance: Open the cut list window and read every row; the rows equal the coffee-table fixture's hand-computed expectations, with identical parts grouped by quantity.

features.title: Open the shopping list and export it
features.acceptance: Open the materials list window, read the stock counts against the fixture's expectations, export it as CSV, and the exported rows match the table on screen.

features.title: Make a drawn box into a part
features.acceptance: Draw a box, name it and say in the properties panel what its third dimension is, which of the three the drawing is showing, how many there are and what stock it is cut from; the panel reports what the library says that stock actually measures before anything is applied, and applying it puts a row on the cut list with the dimensions the stock fixes set from the library and the free ones as drawn.

features.title: Pick stock from the Draw menu and drag it onto the paper
features.acceptance: Ctrl/Cmd+N: Draw > Stock lists the toolbar's categories in its order, each with its icon's tooltip and every size in it; hovering Draw > Stock > Dimensional lumber > 2x4 shows its actual size and citation; clicking it holds the 2x4, closes the menu and opens the lumber drawer reading Holding 2x4; a drag places a 2x4 cut to the dragged 12", selected; the same drag from the drawer's 2x4 places an equal part, each with one value of its own holding it to the 2x4's width; a nail picked from the menu is not held, and the window says fasteners are not placed on the drawing.

features.title: Read the DIY table's cut list with its joinery
features.acceptance: Open the DIY coffee table with drawers from Samples, Ctrl/Cmd+L: thirteen rows and twenty-four pieces in the order its expectations file gives, finished sizes with the joinery allowances in (drawer box front 1'-4 1/8", bottom 1'-4 1/8" x 1'-3 1/2") and every row's joint sentences on screen verbatim, none saying joint not satisfied; a click on the Part header puts the left and right drawer sides next to each other, still two rows of two; the exported CSV has the expectations' two header lines, ending Cuts,Joinery, and the same data lines; opening the plain coffee table leaves four rows with no joinery, and coming back brings the sentences back.

features.title: Place a window on a wall and get a cited header
features.acceptance: Draw a wall, enter what it supports and its site hazard inputs, place an opening on it, and a header size with its code edition, table and row appears.

features.title: Resize the window and watch the header result update
features.acceptance: Drag the opening's edge to widen it across a table row boundary and the displayed header size and citation change to the new row without reopening anything.

features.title: Hit an out-of-scope case
features.acceptance: Keep widening the opening past what the loaded pack's table covers; the result becomes the out-of-scope message with the exceeded limit's citation and no header size is shown at all.

features.title: With the shipped pack's tables not loaded, the check says so
features.acceptance: Choose the shipped Connecticut pack, whose model-code tables are not loaded; the picker labels it 'base tables not loaded' and a window's code check says there is no data and where to add tables, never a size.

features.title: A snow load between two table columns is interpolated, and below the lowest the roof live load decides
features.acceptance: With a synthetic test pack whose header table has two snow-load columns and a footnote, draw an exterior bearing wall, type a snow load between the columns and a roof live load within the footnote's limit in Project > Adopted code and site, then place a window and type its width: the check sizes the header from the interpolated span and shows an interpolation line naming both rows and the footnote, with the weight in the working; a snow load exactly on the lower column uses that row with no interpolation line; a snow load below it with a roof live load over the footnote's limit is out of scope, citing the footnote, with no size.

features.title: Draw a wall, put a window in it, widen it, undo and buy the framing
features.acceptance: Ctrl/Cmd+N, zoom out with the wheel, and W takes the wall tool with 2x4 studs; a drag draws a 12 ft wall on the Wall layer, selected, framed with studs and plates at the design default spacing and a note saying so; Draw > Window and a click centre a 3 ft window in the wall, bound to it, framed with kings, jacks, cripples, a rough sill and a header not yet sized; 4' typed in its width label reframes it with one stud fewer and one cripple more; Ctrl/Cmd+Z puts the 3 ft window and its frame back; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+L shows a framing section that buys 2x4s and lists the header as not yet sized, and its CSV is the rows on screen.

features.title: Open the sample wall, change the spacing, add a door, undo and look in 3D
features.acceptance: Open File > Samples > Wall with window and click the wall away from its window: it reads as a 2x6 wall with the window framed; the next Studs at choice, picked with the pointer, Down and Enter, reframes it with fewer studs and one cripple and drops the design-default note; Draw > Door and a click near the east end stand a door on the floor, and the wall frames both openings with two headers; V shows it in 3D and V comes back; Ctrl/Cmd+Z takes the door away.

features.title: Enlarge an opening until the bracing check flags it
features.acceptance: With the bracing method already on each of the wall line's segments entered, widen the opening step by step until the wall line is flagged, and the flag names the section applied and the shortfall.

features.title: Change the project's adopted code and see results recomputed
features.acceptance: Open the project's code picker, switch it to the other installed pack, and every rules result on screen recomputes with citations naming the newly chosen code.

features.title: A result that no longer holds is re-flagged, not carried over
features.acceptance: After the code change, a result that no longer holds under the new pack (an opening it does not cover, or a wall line whose bracing now runs short or uses a method the new pack does not have) is re-flagged rather than keeping what the old pack produced, and the message bar says how many results changed, became flagged or can no longer be computed.

features.title: With the shipped pack, the bracing check says there is no data
features.acceptance: Choose the shipped Connecticut pack, which has no wall-bracing provisions; a wall's Bracing block lists its segments with disabled method pickers that say why, and its check says there is no data and where to add it, never a length.

features.title: Tool buttons show a tooltip
features.acceptance: Hovering the Select or Rectangle tool button shows a tooltip naming the tool and its keyboard shortcut.

features.title: Relationship glyphs show their sentence on hover
features.acceptance: Hovering a relationship glyph on the canvas (e.g. a flush indicator) shows the same plain-language sentence as its row in the relationship list.

features.title: Rough mode snaps one rung coarser and states nothing it catches
features.acceptance: The rough step is the rung above the precise step, never below 1 inch, on the ladder and a multiple of the precise step up to 48 inches; a rough drag lands on it; a rough drop still catches another part's edge but adds no relationship, where a precise drop adds one.

features.title: A rough rectangle is a plank
features.acceptance: The rectangle tool in Rough mode makes a box whose part has no stock, no species, quantity 1, its longer plan side the length, marked rough, 3/4 inch deep; in Precise the box has no part, as before.

features.title: Sketch a quick bench roughly
features.acceptance: Press Q: the status bar reads ROUGH and the toolbar shows Rough; draw the four parts of the quick bench a little off the round numbers; each lands on whole inches as a rough plank, nothing is stated though a leg was dragged against the top; the selected leg's labels wait until the pointer is over it; the status bar reads its name and three sizes.

features.title: Firm up a rough bench and read its cut list
features.acceptance: With the quick bench sketched rough, F opens Firm up listing its four contacts, four stock lines and four size lines, all ticked; untick one relationship with the pointer and press Enter: three Flushes land, every part is firm and cut from its nearest stock, in one undo step; Ctrl+Z makes all four rough again with nothing stated; Ctrl+Y; the cut list opened from the menu has no rough row and the rows worked out by hand.

features.title: Type a size on a rough part
features.acceptance: Draw one plank rough; its labels are quiet until the pointer is over it; click the width label, type 3'-0" and press Enter: the width is exactly 36 inches and the part is no longer rough; one undo restores both the width and the rough mark.

features.title: Rough on the cut list, and the mark by hand
features.acceptance: Draw two planks rough; the cut list tags both rows rough and says two rows are; select one, untick Rough in the Part panel with the pointer, Tab, Enter: the undo step is 'mark firm', the cut list has one rough row, and the CSV says yes on that row only.

features.title: The canvas exposes one automation element per part
features.acceptance: Every Box in the Sketch is reachable as a distinct automation element under the canvas, with a name, a read-only size value, and a bounding rectangle that follows pan/zoom/edits — proven by querying Avalonia's own automation peer tree in-process, not a screenshot.

features.title: A joint is a relationship between two faces the updater neither propagates nor refuses
features.acceptance: A Joint names one face of each of two parts; moving or resizing a part with a joint is Solved and leaves the joint as it was; the checker never lists a joint; the joint is unsatisfied (not refused) once the two faces no longer share a rectangle, or when its depth is not less than the receiving thickness; removing either part removes the joint.

features.title: Format version 5 carries joints, hardware, fastener choices and supplies
features.acceptance: A joint, a part's hardware, the fastener choices and the supplies lines round-trip byte for byte through the writer and reader; every refusal row of the joinery note section 4.4 is refused naming its field; a version-4 file is refused with the unsupported-version message.

features.title: A joint's two boxes imply its contact, groove, rabbet and half-lap, and which part receives
features.acceptance: Derived from the drawn boxes and never stored: the contact rectangle of two faces (apron end on a leg: 3/4 x 5 1/2), a groove along the length (drawer bottom in a side: 1/4 wide, 1/2 from the bottom edge) or a dado across the width, a rabbet at the nearer end, a half-lap overlap and each part's lap; and the direction rule of note 4.1 (inserted part is the one whose contact face is an end, the thinner for a groove, the top for a tabletop, lower id first for a half-lap, larger part receiving when it cannot decide).

features.title: Joinery allowances and the fixed joint sentences are in the cut list
features.acceptance: A part inserted into a groove or rabbet lists its drawn size plus the depth at each grooved edge or rabbeted end (drawer box front 16000 -> 16512, bottom 16000 x 15360 -> 16512 x 15872); each groove, dado, rabbet, half-lap, run of pocket holes and set of tabletop clips reads as the note 6.2 sentence, in the part's own frame.

features.title: Joinery is in the group key, up to a half-turn of the part
features.acceptance: Four legs and the two side aprons (pocket holes from opposite faces at opposite ends) are one row each; left and right drawer sides are two rows; two parts equal but for a groove depth are two rows.

features.title: An unsatisfied joint keeps its allowance and flags the row
features.acceptance: A joint whose parts moved apart still lengthens the inserted part and says nothing that needs a contact; the row says joint not satisfied; a depth not less than the receiving thickness adds no allowance.

features.title: The CSV has a Joinery column and the new header line
features.acceptance: The first line reads finished sizes: joinery allowances included; before saw kerf (#138); the header ends Cuts,Joinery; the Joinery column parses back to the rows' sentences, followed by joint not satisfied on a flagged row.

features.title: Fastener recipes give the counts the sentences read
features.acceptance: Pocket screws max(2, ceil(L/2)), screws 6, brads 1.5, nails 4, dowels 4, biscuits max(1, ceil(L/8)), clips max(2, ceil(L/12)); a typed count overrides.

features.title: The fastener list sums the joints' fasteners by kind and typed size
features.acceptance: Counts by (kind, thickness) in kind order then thickness descending; the size is the person's typed choice and a missing choice says size not chosen; packs are ceil(count / pack size); each line names its joints; the sample gives 27, 6, 8, 24 and 10.

features.title: Hardware, supplies and the glue line join the shopping list
features.acceptance: Hardware sums quantity times part quantity by exact name; supplies are the typed lines plus Glue: N of M joints; fasteners, hardware and supplies are rows below the boards, in a CSV with columns Section,Item,Size,Count,Pack,Packs,For that equals the rows on screen.

features.title: The join tool proposes the faces, the type, the direction and the pocket face
features.acceptance: For two touching parts: the largest contact between faces that face each other; overlap of one thickness laps, a bottom face on a long thin contact is a tabletop, a thinner part's edge entering a face with margin is a groove, else a butt; pocket holes default to the inserted part's broad face nearer the middle of everything, both offered on a tie.

features.title: Firm up proposes the relationships touching parts imply
features.acceptance: For each pair of the given parts that touch over an area, older id first: one Flush per pair of faces facing each other, and one per pair of X or Y faces facing the same way at one coordinate whose other extents meet; none for parts that do not touch, overlap, or are walls; none already held in either order; ordered by pair, against before alongside, axis, then face; each accepted by the updater without moving anything.

features.title: A joint reads as one sentence: type, parts, depth, fasteners with their typed size, glue
features.acceptance: Rabbet, Drawer side, left, A from Drawer box front, A: 1/4 deep, 1/2 wide, 3 brads with the chosen size or size not chosen, glue; parts that no longer touch say so and drop the recipe count.

features.title: Join two parts with J, read the marker and its tooltip, edit and delete it
features.acceptance: Draw two parts, refusal messages for one part and for two that do not touch, J, Enter makes a butt with a solid marker in plan and 3D; the tooltip reads as one sentence; double-click or Enter reopens it; Delete removes it and undo brings it back.

features.title: Join the leg frame in one gesture with Shift+J
features.acceptance: Nine selected parts give ten touching pairs, pairs of another suggested type are unticked, pocket screws chosen with the keys, the web's tied pocket face picked, one Enter makes ten joints and one undo removes them.

features.title: Join a drawer: rabbet with a typed depth, groove pre-selected, typed count over the recipe
features.acceptance: A rabbet needs a depth and says so; the bottom's groove is pre-selected; the count box shows recipe: 3 and 4 typed over it is kept; Shift+J on two parts repeats the last joint.

features.title: Move a joined part: markers go hollow, the cut-list row is flagged, undo restores
features.acceptance: Nothing is refused and nothing follows the move; two markers are hollow, the tooltip says the parts no longer touch, the rows say joint not satisfied, one undo puts it all back.

features.title: Type a fastener size and watch the shopping list change
features.acceptance: Blank sizes first; a typed size and pack update the fastener line and packs; a bad pack size is refused in words; a size nobody needs survives saving; undo restores.

features.title: Type hardware on a part and supplies on the list, and export them
features.acceptance: The Part panel's hardware box, Ctrl+Enter, the hardware section summed, supplies typed with notes, the glue line, the CSV equal to the screen, undo.

features.title: Join the whole table and read the cut list and the fasteners
features.acceptance: The storyboard on the DIY table: frame, cleats, both drawers, tabletop, all 34 joints as the sample records them, 13 cut-list rows, sizes and supplies typed, 27 / 6 / 8 / 24 / 10 fasteners.

features.title: A DIY coffee table with drawers, from stock to cut list
features.acceptance: Ctrl/Cmd+N, then with only the pointer and keyboard: the top, legs, aprons, rail, web and one drawer are placed from stock and sized, mirrored (M, Shift+M) and copied (D); Shift+J and J join them with pocket-screwed butts, grooves, rabbets, brads and tabletop clips and a typed screw count; the drawer is mirrored with its joints and a pull typed on its front, for 22 parts and 32 joints; in 3D the Z and Y buttons look from above and from the front; Ctrl/Cmd+L's cut list and its CSV are the twelve rows worked out by hand, with finished sizes and joinery sentences; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+L buys boards and sheets and counts 27 pocket screws, 8 wood screws, 24 brads, 10 clips, the pull and the glue for 18 of 32 joints; a typed pocket-screw size and pack size come to one pack; and Ctrl/Cmd+S, Ctrl/Cmd+N, Ctrl/Cmd+O bring back the same 22 parts and cut list.

features.title: The cut layout puts each lumber piece on a board with the saw kerf
features.acceptance: Per stock and species the pieces go longest first onto boards opened at the longest stocked length, then each board shrinks to the smallest stocked length that holds it; a board takes n cuts when an offcut remains and n-1 when the pieces and kerfs exactly fill it; a piece longer than any stocked length is refused by name; sheet goods are reported as counted by sheets, not nested. 36 + 24 + 20 in on a 96 in board with a 1/8 in kerf is 80 3/8 in used and a 15 5/8 in offcut.

features.title: The shopping list's boards are the cut layout's boards
features.acceptance: The shopping list takes its board counts from the cut layout with the kerf given, so the two never disagree; the stocked bench needs one 12 ft 1x4 and one 14 ft 2x4 at a 1/8 in kerf.

features.title: Firm up suggests the stock a rough part is nearest
features.acceptance: StockSuggestion lists library items whose every fixed dimension is within 1 inch of the part's finished size: items fixing more dimensions first, then the smallest total difference, then the name; a part near nothing gets none; a fastener never appears; the values are the library's.

features.title: Rough rows are tagged on the cut list, the CSV and the shopping list
features.acceptance: A cut-list row is rough when any member is; roughness is not in the grouping key; the table tags it and says how many rows are rough; the CSV has a Rough column (yes or empty) after Material and says rough rows are as drawn; the shopping list says how many rough parts have no stock and are not on it.

features.title: The Parts view's sheet is the cut list, one cell per row
features.acceptance: For every sample, PartsSheet.Of(CutList.Of(sketch)) has one cell per row, in row order, each cell's row the row itself and its count the row's quantity; the blank a cell draws is the piece in its own frame in all 24 orientations, and the cut list's thumbnails draw the same blank.

features.title: The Parts view's counts add up to pieces, not boxes
features.acceptance: For every sample the cells' counts sum to the sum of Part.Quantity over boxes with a part; the coffee table's four legs are one cell of 4 and each apron length one cell of 2.

features.title: A Parts view cell shows its piece at the sheet's one scale, or says it is not to scale
features.acceptance: A piece is drawn flat, on edge, face-on (on end, no cuts: a leg, length x width) or on end (with cuts), its longer side across, captioned with the dimension it does not show; the sheet's scale is the largest at which every piece fits 224 x 100 px (the coffee table's is 100/24 px/in); a piece whose longer side would draw under 48 px is drawn at 48 px and says not to scale (scale-extremes' shim, 8 px/in); a cell says its count and at most two cuts before how many more.

features.title: The Parts sheet is a wrapped grid of equal cells, grouped under title bands, on whole pixels
features.acceptance: Columns are what the width buys at the zoom and never fewer than one (1, 2, 4 at 300, 560, 1100 px at 100 %); cells fill rows in the sheet's order and never overlap; a group starts its own row under a 24 px title band; every edge is a whole pixel; a cell reads to a screen reader as its label, count, three sizes and material.

features.title: A Parts cell reads the design's one selection: all, partly or none, and how many boxes its pieces are
features.acceptance: A cell is selected when every member is, partly when some are, not otherwise, whatever else is selected; a cell whose count and box count differ says 4 pieces from 1 box or 3 pieces from 2 boxes, and says nothing when they agree.

features.title: Read the cut layout and change the saw kerf
features.acceptance: Open a sample, open the cut list, turn to the Cut layout tab, see a line and a drawn bar per board, change the saw kerf and see the boards change, and the exported file equals the lines on screen.

features.title: The drawer readout names what is held right after a menu pick
features.acceptance: Ctrl/Cmd+N, then Draw > Stock > Dimensional lumber > 2x4 with the mouse and no further pointer move: the 2x4 is held, the lumber drawer is open, and its readout says Holding 2x4, not the hover text of the drawer item that opened under the pointer.

features.title: A cut-list row selects its parts in the drawing
features.acceptance: Coffee table, Ctrl/Cmd+L: a click on the Leg row selects the four legs; Shift on the Top row adds the top; Ctrl/Cmd on the Leg row takes the legs out; a header click sorts and selects nothing; another row replaces the selection; in 3D it is the same selection and Escape clears it.

features.title: The six standard views look along exact axes
features.acceptance: StandardViews.Axes gives standard-views §1.1's table exactly for Top, Bottom, Front, Back, Left and Right, right-handed (Right x Up = TowardViewer); CameraFor's camera has exactly those vectors (no 1e-16 from cos 90), is orthographic, keeps centre and scale, and looks the same way as the matching 3D view-snap direction.

features.title: Front of the l-bracket and the coffee table, measured
features.acceptance: In Front the l-bracket spans 7 1/2 x 6; the lug is left of the boss, 4 1/2 in from its left edge and 3 1/4 in higher; the nub is leftmost and the tab rightmost. The coffee table spans 48 x 17 and each of its four legs is exactly 16 1/4 tall.

features.title: Keys 1-7 name the views; modified digits do not
features.acceptance: Unmodified 1-7 on the top row or the number pad give Top, Bottom, Front, Back, Left, Right and 3D; Cmd/Ctrl/Shift+digit, 0, 8 and other keys give none; standard views and design views map one to one by name.

features.title: Settings version 2 keeps every view; version 1 is refused
features.acceptance: Every one of the seven DesignView values round-trips as LastView through settings.json version 2; a version-1 file (LastView "Plan") is refused with a notice naming its version and the defaults apply (Top).

features.title: The standard views' frame: axes, names, readable coordinates
features.acceptance: StandardViewFrame gives every view its section 1.1 axes as signed world axes, right-handed, its name, whether it is an elevation, and the two coordinates its readout shows (x y in Top/Bottom, x z in Front/Back, y z in Left/Right).

features.title: All six views of the l-bracket and the coffee table, hand-derived
features.acceptance: Extents 7.5x5, 7.5x6, 5x6; Back mirrors Front (nub rightmost, tab leftmost); Right has the boss left of the upright, the lug leftmost and the rib rightmost; Left the rib leftmost; Bottom the lug above the rib; the coffee table's Front equals Back mirrored and Left equals Right; every leg is 16 1/4 tall in all four elevations.

features.title: Hidden edges: each face's edges less what a strictly nearer face covers
features.acceptance: HiddenEdges.Split on hand-drawn faces: flush squares hide nothing; nearer by more than 1/2048 inch hides, by less does not; a corner overlap hides exactly its quarter; a notch in a nearer outline lets the edge show through; an outline exactly behind another shows no dash; a dash is dropped only where a solid edge lies along it; rulings and zero-length edges get no line; a tilted face hides only where nearer everywhere.

features.title: One table of drawing line kinds and weights
features.acceptance: DrawingLines: visible heavier than hidden heavier than dimension (= extension); hidden is 1 px, dash [3,3], 0.35; the others solid but the centre chain; every kind has a line. A hidden dash is lighter than a visible edge yet at least 1.15:1 on every layer's flat fill, light, dark and napkin.

features.title: Hidden edges on the l-bracket and the coffee table; the setting
features.acceptance: Front: lug whole, rib dashed (one 1/2-inch dash at z 2); Back the reverse; Right tab whole, nub dashed; Left nub whole, tab dashed; Bottom skid whole, boss dashed. Coffee table Front dashes only each short apron's inner side and bottom (z 12 3/4 to 16 1/4, 3/4 wide, inside a near leg). ShowHiddenEdges is on by default and remembered.

features.title: Dimensions per standard view, laid out in its plane
features.acceptance: A view shows a dimension along its screen-right or screen-up axis (X,Y in Top/Bottom; X in Front/Back; Y in Left/Right); South/West low, North/East high with the plan's fallback. Coffee table: 6, 6, 4, 4, 2, 2 by name; every label is Top's; Top is the plan's layout; Front's top width lies at z 12 1/4 (4 below the top); Back runs right to left; Bottom's South line is on the screen-up side; the inset (North, 1) lies at z 18; a short apron (West, 2) at z 10 3/4.

features.title: Rulers and grid of a standard view in world values
features.acceptance: ViewGrid: a mirrored axis shows the same world span counted the other way; grid lines on the plan's ladder, heavy on the next step; an elevation's floor (z = 0) heavy even with no heavier step; no lines for a bad or huge span. StandardViewRulers on the l-bracket: Back's and Left's horizontal rulers count down, Bottom's vertical counts down upward, Front's and Right's rise both ways; the tick at x 6 1/2 sits where the camera projects it in Front and Back; the floor line in Front is heavy and in place.

features.title: The standard views' sentences come from one Module type
features.acceptance: StandardViewWords: the read-only hint and the not-in-this-view refusal name the view; the three hidden-edge sentences are fixed. GUI tests compare against these, not copies.

features.title: Switch between Top, Front and 3D by key, chip and menu
features.acceptance: Open the l-bracket; 3 shows Front (orthographic, lug up-left of the boss), 7 shows 3D, V returns to Front and V twice lands back; the Top, 3D and Front chips and View > Standard views > Front do the same; after each the status text, the pressed chip and the menu tick agree; 4 shows Back and says it is read-only, and O leaves it orthographic.

features.title: Front is read-only: pan, zoom and select
features.acceptance: In Front the rectangle tool is disabled with a tooltip and the turn and snap buttons are hidden; a click selects the lug with no handles; a drag on it pans and changes nothing; the left arrow pans; Home fits; Delete removes the selected lug and Undo brings it back, still in Front.

features.title: A digit typed as a length is not a view
features.acceptance: After dragging an arrow in 3D, 3 goes into the typed length (the view stays 3D) and Enter moves the part exactly 3 in; with no length pending, 3 shows Front.

features.title: The tool keys work in 3D and say why not in a standard view
features.acceptance: Open the coffee table, select the south apron and press 7: R holds a plain board to place, S puts it down and is the select tool, still in 3D; 3 then C says the workshop is not in Front yet and opens nothing; W brings the plan forward with the wall tool.

features.title: All six views by key, chip and menu, each with its own camera and a two-coordinate readout
features.acceptance: Open the l-bracket; 2 shows Bottom (lug above rib), the Back chip shows Back (nub right of tab), 5 shows Left (rib left of lug) and the pointer on the nub reads y 2 1/2 z 3 3/8 with no x; View > Standard views > Right shows Right (boss left of upright); a pan in Right survives a trip to Front; 7 reads three coordinates again; the six views draw six different pictures.

features.title: Hidden edges toggle by menu and by H, kept across windows
features.acceptance: Open the l-bracket; in the plan the item is disabled and H says where hidden edges are drawn; 3 shows Front with them ticked and the rib dashed; View > Hidden edges turns them off and only pixels on the rib's dash change; H turns them back on to the same picture; off again, a new window on the same settings has them off.

features.title: Each view of the coffee table draws its dimensions and follows an edit
features.acceptance: Open the coffee table; 3 draws the four X dimensions, the top's width below the top; 5 the two Y ones; the Bottom chip all six; in Top, Tab 50 Enter widens the top; 4 shows 4'-2" at once; 7 draws none.

features.title: Rulers and grid in Back count down, follow a pan, and step with the zoom
features.acceptance: Open the l-bracket; 4 then View > Rulers: labels on both rulers, the top one descending, the toolbar stepped in, no scale bar, the floor a heavy grid line; the right arrow pans and the numbers move, still descending; a 40 px drag moves every tick 40 px; a wheel zoom out steps the ladder up; 7 shows no rulers.

features.title: The sheet's arrangement and shared scale are pure
features.acceptance: SheetLayout puts Top above Front and Right beside Front, 3D in the spare corner, in equal panes with a gutter; SharedScale is the scale the tightest drawing fits at. The sheet's hint, refusal and projection note come from StandardViewWords.

features.title: A grid that fades with zoom instead of crowding
features.acceptance: GridLevels over 0.5 % to 20 000 %: every drawn level is 10-200 px apart below the ladder's top; exactly two levels (the snap step and a heavier step above it on the ladder), one at the top; zooming in never coarsens a level; the minor level fades from 0.35 at 14 px to full at 28 px and never below; the major is always full; a 3D ground line fades from full at the middle to 0.35 at the edge.

features.title: The sheet shows Top over Front and Right beside it, at one scale, selection shared, remembered
features.acceptance: Open the l-bracket; View > Sheet: four captioned panes in third-angle order, the three drawings at one scale so x lines up in Top and Front and z in Front and Right; a click on the upright in Front draws it selected in every pane; R says not on the sheet; 3 leaves for Front alone and forgets the sheet; View > Sheet brings it back, remembered, the upright still selected.

features.title: The Parts view shows the coffee table's pieces, one cell each, and walks them by keyboard and pointer
features.acceptance: Open the coffee table from Samples; View > Parts: four cells, the top x1, the legs x4 and two apron cells x2, the Parts chip pressed and its hint said; Right, Right, Down move the focus cell along and down a row; a click focuses the legs' cell; R says not in the Parts view; View > Zoom in shows 125 %; 7 then V returns to Top, never to Parts; the Parts chip shows it again; 3 leaves for Front.

features.title: Selection runs both ways between the Parts view and the model
features.acceptance: A click on the coffee table's legs cell selects the four legs; 3D shows them selected; back in Parts the cell is selected; Escape clears; Home, Right, Right, Enter selects them from the keyboard; one leg picked in Front leaves the cell partly selected, drawn dashed.

features.title: Deleting one leg from the Parts view reads x3, and undo x4, as the cut list does
features.acceptance: One leg picked in Front; in the Parts view Delete takes it and the legs cell reads x3; Cmd/Ctrl+Z reads x4 again; the cut list opened afterwards says four legs.

features.title: The Parts view's grouping and 3D choice are remembered, and a new window opens in them
features.acceptance: Open the stocked bench in the Parts view; View > Group parts by stock: groups 3/4 plywood, 1x4, 2x4 under title bands, the keyboard walking them in screen order; View > Parts in 3D; a new window on the same settings opens in the Parts view, grouped, in 3D, both menu items ticked.

features.title: A setting changed from the View menu is kept by a new window
features.acceptance: Open the coffee table: a fresh run has rulers off and perspective; View > Rulers, then V and O, write rulers on and orthographic to the settings file as they are made; a new window on the same settings file starts with rulers drawn, View > Rulers ticked and the 3D view orthographic.

features.title: Choosing a theme from the View menu recolours the plan and the 3D view
features.acceptance: Open the coffee table: the window follows the system by default, light here, and View > Appearance > Theme says so; Dark darkens the window and the plan's paper, is ticked and remembered, and V shows the 3D view on dark paper too; Light puts the same plan back on light paper; Follow system returns to the system's theme and is remembered as that choice.

features.title: Hiding the grid does not stop snapping, and snapping off does not hide the grid
features.acceptance: Open the coffee table: the grid shows and snapping is on by default, and the status bar names the step; View > Grid hides the lines and is remembered with snapping untouched, and a rectangle drawn with R still lands on the grid; View > Snap to grid turns snapping off with the grid still hidden, the step leaves the status bar, and the next rectangle is off the grid; G then V shows the grid in the plan and on the 3D ground with snapping still off, G in 3D hides the ground grid, and a new window on the same settings has no grid and no snapping.

features.title: Designs open in the view chosen from the menu
features.acceptance: Last used is the default and ticked; Project > Open designs in > 3D leaves the view on screen alone and the next sample opens in 3D, even after V back to the plan; 2D plan leaves the 3D view on screen and the next sample opens on the plan; Last used opens the next sample in the view last left, 3D; with 3D chosen again, a new window on the same settings has it ticked and opens a new sheet in 3D.

features.title: Choosing paper and pencil from the View menu redraws both views and changes nothing else
features.acceptance: Open the coffee table in the clean screen look, ticked; View > Appearance > Paper and line > Graph paper, then Pencil, put the plan and the 3D view on graph paper in pencil, ticked and remembered; Plain sheet, then Napkin with Carpenter's pencil, redraw both views; a rectangle drawn with R under the look is a real part; Screen and Clean bring the original paper back and are remembered.

features.title: The default napkin look keeps the bench chrome and the sheet the same in light and dark
features.acceptance: In the default look the coffee table opens on the napkin sheet in carpenter's pencil, with the menu bar and status bar in the bench colour; View > Appearance > Theme > Dark leaves the menu bar, the status bar and the napkin unchanged; back in Light, View > Appearance > Paper and line > Screen and Clean bring back the theme-following paper under the same bench chrome.

features.title: The last view is remembered; 2D plan opens Top
features.acceptance: With Open designs in > Last used, press 3; the next design opens in Front, and so does a new window on the same settings; choose Open designs in > 2D plan and the next design opens on Top.

features.title: Mark a wall existing and put a new window in it
features.acceptance: Draw a wall; mark it Existing from Edit > Phase, then New and Existing again from the panel's picker; say it is exterior and bearing; put a window in it: the message bar and the wall's panel say new - 2 king studs, 2 jack studs, header, sill, 2 cripples; out - 2 studs, assuming a regular 16" layout; undo takes the window and then the phase back.

features.title: Draw a room and read its area takeoff
features.acceptance: Open the basement sample and pick its room: four bounding walls, both openings, 18 sheets and 10 bags; on a new sheet press Shift+W and click; type 14' and 12' on the room's labels; pick drywall on walls and ceiling, type a 4' x 8' sheet, tick the floor and type a 20 sq ft box: the shopping list's Area takeoff says 19 sheets and 10 boxes, and its CSV carries it.

features.title: Put rough-in notes and count them
features.acceptance: Press Shift+N and click three times, typing outlet, switch and sump pit; outlet and switch take their symbols, and the drain glyph is picked for the sump pit with the pointer; the shopping list's Notes line reads outlet x 1, switch x 1, drain x 1; pick the switch and press Delete: the line loses it.

features.title: Finish a basement room end to end
features.acceptance: Draw the four walls of the 12 x 14 ft room to exact sizes and say each is exterior, not bearing, with a (2) 2x6 header; put in the door and the window; click a room inside the walls and tick its finishes; put six notes; the shopping list buys 2x4 1 x 6', 3 x 12', 1 x 14', 31 x 16' and 2x6 1 x 14', 18 drywall sheets, and counts outlet x 4, switch x 1, light x 1; mark the west wall existing: two of its studs come out under Demolition; undo.

features.title: Existing drawn faint, demolish dashed and crossed
features.acceptance: Mark a wall Existing from the Edit menu, put a new window in it, then Demolish the wall from the panel with the keyboard: plan and 3D draw it faint, then long-dashed and crossed; the shopping list says only New is listed and counts the wall and its frame under Demolition; undo.
